summary: Eiichi Yamaguchi is an indologist and philosopher. A graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990), he served there as a research assistant (attested 1990–1991).
Eiju Fukushima works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. As attested in 2026, he held faculty posts at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.
Eikan Taki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a member of Taisho University and served as a lecturer (講師) at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).
Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962–1972). He later served there as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (~1985–2014).
Eiko Okukaze is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010). He is attested as a commissioned researcher (受託研究員) at Koyasan University in 2026.

Eileen Power was a historian who studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1907–1910) and the University of Paris (~1910–1911). She held posts at the London School of Economics and the University of London (~1921–1940).

Eisaku Okada, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and held posts at the JSPS (attested 2014), Kyoto University (attested 2015), and Koyasan University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as president (学長) of Doho University and as a professor (教授) at Ryukoku University (both attested 1976).

Eishu Miyazaki was a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Rissho University (~1933–1938) under Gyoo Kageyama, later holding posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1949–1984).
Eishun Fushimi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
Eivind Kahrs is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2010), and is a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eiyin Yasuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1956–1960) and was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto.
Eizan Tatsuta was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College. He served as rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji (~1891) and professor at Toyo University (1916).
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010) and is a faculty member at Stanford University (attested 2026).

Eleanor Nesbitt is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Oxford. She served as professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989–2012).

Eleanor Rosch studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Roger Brown. She held positions at Connecticut College, Brown University, and was a professor of cognitive psychology at UC Berkeley from 1971.

Elena Bashir is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan until 1988. She has held posts at the University of Chicago, including in 2000 and as an editorial board member (attested 2026).
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian history under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome (graduated 1971), where she became an associate professor in 1980.
